title: Natural reconstruction comparisons for the integral tower adjunction
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. On the small pro-etale sites put $R_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T$, $B_{n,T}=(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T$, for $T=X,Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $\mathcal C_T=\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ for the derived-complete bounded constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and $\mathcal N_T$ for the full subcategory of normalized constructible strict varying-coefficient towers with common cohomological and Tor bounds [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Put $r_TA=(A\otimes^L_{R_T}B_{n,T})_n$ and $L_T=R\varprojlim\operatorname{Res}$, the total derived limit after restriction of scalars to $R_T$ [det-sp-normalized-equivalence].

Choose a compactification $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j$ open and $\bar f$ proper, and put $F=R\bar f_*j_!$ [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower]. Use $F_\bullet=Rf_{!,\bullet}$ and $G_\bullet=f^!_\bullet$, with the specified tower adjunction and its unit $\eta^\bullet$ and counit $\varepsilon^\bullet$ [det-sp-tower-gluing]. Then $X,Y$ are Noetherian, $r_T:\mathcal C_T\to\mathcal N_T$ is fully faithful with inverse $L_T$, and $F_\bullet,G_\bullet$ restrict to an adjunction $\mathcal N_X\rightleftarrows\mathcal N_Y$, whose unit and counit are the same actual tower maps as in the ambient tower categories.

The assignment $H(K)=L_XG_\bullet r_YK$ is a functor $\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_X$, and there are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$b_M:r_YFM\xrightarrow{\sim}F_\bullet r_XM,\qquad c_K:r_XH(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}G_\bullet r_YK.$$
Here $c_K$ is the counit of $r_X\dashv L_X$ at $G_\bullet r_YK$, and $b_M$ is the entire-tower direct-image comparison induced by the compactification, not merely a collection of levelwise isomorphisms. For $a:M\to M'$ and $h:K\to K'$, their naturality equations are
$$F_\bullet r_X(a)b_M=b_{M'}r_YF(a),\qquad G_\bullet r_Y(h)c_K=c_{K'}r_XH(h).$$
Let $u_A:A\xrightarrow{\sim}L_Tr_TA$ be the actual reconstruction unit. For every morphism $a:A\to B$ in $\mathcal C_T$ one has the equality of actual morphisms
$$a=u_B^{-1}L_T(r_Ta)u_A.$$
In particular this reconstruction formula applies to any unit or counit obtained by restricting the specified tower adjunction along $b,c$.

source.place: Normalization and Bijections: normalization, natural direct-image and exceptional reconstruction comparisons, and restriction to full normalized subcategories

proof.text: Every ideal of the field $k$ is either $0$ or $(1)$, so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the structure maps of $X,Y$, and then to the proper (hence finite-type) map $\bar f$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus $X,Y,\bar X$ are Noetherian and in particular quasi-compact. They are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Apply [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target] to $X\xrightarrow j\bar X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ to see that $j$ is quasi-compact. The scalar $\ell$ is invertible on all three schemes since $p\ne\ell$. These verify the geometric hypotheses used below.

source.place: Normalization: Noetherian hypothesis of the constructible equivalence; compactification geometry (Stacks 01T6, 01OY)

proof.text: Apply [det-sp-normalized-equivalence] to $T=X,Y$. Its coefficient ring is exactly $R_T=\lim B_{n,T}$, its category is the derived-complete category specified here, and its normalized subcategory has the same common cohomological and Tor bounds. It supplies $r_T\dashv L_T$, with actual natural unit $u$ and counit $e$, invertible on $\mathcal C_T$ and $\mathcal N_T$ respectively, and restricts to the equivalence $\mathcal C_T\simeq\mathcal N_T$. In particular $r_T$ is fully faithful and $L_T$ is its inverse on these full subcategories. In Lean the chosen LimitPresentation may have a different adjunction on the same reduction and total-limit functors. Uniqueness of right and left adjoints transports invertibility of the normalized-equivalence unit and counit to this actual presentation. The intrinsic/augmented completeness comparison [lem-sf-derived-complete-legacy-comparison] verifies the unit hypothesis. Restrict this adjunction with Mathlib Adjunction.restrictFullyFaithful and invert its unit and counit to form the recorded equivalences, with the exact red and lim functors.

source.place: Normalization: equivalence, full faithfulness, actual unit and counit

proof.text: By [det-sp-tower-gamma](3), $F_\bullet$ and $G_\bullet$ both preserve $\mathcal N$. Restrict the natural Hom bijection of the specified adjunction [det-sp-tower-gluing] to $C\in\mathcal N_X$, $D\in\mathcal N_Y$. By fullness [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], its two Hom sets are exactly those in the normalized categories. This gives $F_\bullet|_{\mathcal N_X}\dashv G_\bullet|_{\mathcal N_Y}$. Its unit is the ambient transpose of $1_{F_\bullet C}$ and its counit the ambient inverse transpose of $1_{G_\bullet D}$; hence they are the original actual tower arrows. Their naturality and triangle equations are unchanged equations in the same Hom sets.

source.place: Normalization and Bijections: preserve normalized objects and restrict the specified adjunction

proof.text: For $K\in\mathcal C_Y$, step 2 puts $r_YK\in\mathcal N_Y$, step 3 puts $N_K=G_\bullet r_YK\in\mathcal N_X$, and step 2 puts $L_XN_K\in\mathcal C_X$. Define $H=L_XG_\bullet r_Y$ on morphisms by this composite of functors; identities and compositions are preserved by each factor. Set $c_K=e_{N_K}:r_XH(K)\to N_K$. It is invertible by step 2. Naturality of this same counit gives $G_\bullet r_Y(h)c_K=c_{K'}r_XL_XG_\bullet r_Y(h)=c_{K'}r_XH(h)$.

source.place: Normalization: construct H and its actual counit comparison

proof.text:
For $M\in\mathcal C_X$ put $D_M=F_\bullet r_XM\in\mathcal N_Y$ by steps 2–3. The unit at $M$ is invertible and the levels of $r_XM$ share a lower cohomological bound [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Exact evaluation commutes with derived homology [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Evaluations jointly detect zero strict semilinear systems [def-pur-system-level-left-extension-basic], and the recorded ordinary equivalence is faithful, so the cohomology tower below that bound has every level zero and is zero. Thus $r_XM$ is bounded below in the tower derived category. For the chosen compactification, $F_\bullet=Rf_{!,\bullet}$ is by definition $Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$ (with $p=\bar f$) on bounded-below towers [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels], so $D_M=Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}r_XM$. With step 1, these are all the hypotheses of [lem-sp-complete-compactification-limit-realization]. Its canonical natural isomorphism is $\alpha_M:FM\xrightarrow{\sim}L_YD_M$, formed from $F(u_M)$, open extension/total-limit, proper direct-image/total-limit and scalar-restriction comparisons, with the actual quotient projections. Step 2 gives $L_YD_M\in\mathcal C_Y$; hence $FM$ also lies in this full subcategory, whose defining conditions are invariant under isomorphism [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated]. Define
$$b_M=e_{D_M}\circ r_Y(\alpha_M):r_YFM\xrightarrow{\sim}D_M.$$
This is an isomorphism of entire derived strict towers, built from the specified $\alpha_M$ followed after reduction by the specified reconstruction counit; no arrow is assembled from levelwise data.

source.place: Bijections, first comparison: construct the whole-tower direct-image isomorphism

proof.text:
For $a:M\to M'$, naturality of $\alpha$ says $L_Y(D_a)\alpha_M=\alpha_{M'}F(a)$, where $D_a=F_\bullet r_X(a)$. Naturality of $e$ says $D_a e_{D_M}=e_{D_{M'}}r_YL_Y(D_a)$. Substituting the first equality into the second after composition with $r_Y\alpha_M$ gives
$$F_\bullet r_X(a)b_M=e_{D_{M'}}r_Y(\alpha_{M'})r_YF(a)=b_{M'}r_YF(a).$$
Together with step 4 this proves both required naturality equations as actual tower morphism equations.

source.place: Bijections: naturality in both variables of the reconstruction comparisons

proof.text:
For any $a:A\to B$ in $\mathcal C_T$, naturality of the actual reconstruction unit from step 2 is $L_T(r_Ta)u_A=u_Ba$. Compose on the left with the inverse of the invertible $u_B$ to obtain
$$a=u_B^{-1}L_T(r_Ta)u_A.$$
This equality holds for every morphism of $\mathcal C_T$, including the units and counits when the specified tower adjunction is restricted along the natural isomorphisms $b,c$. It uses the actual unit, rather than any chosen isomorphism $A\simeq L_Tr_TA$.

source.place: Bijections: reconstruct the actual unit/counit morphisms by naturality
